name: ANSI/IEEE crossing conductor hop symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented hop or loop drawn where one conductor passes over another without connecting.
description: Older ANSI-style schematics often draw a small semicircular hop where one conductor crosses another, removing any doubt that the two are unconnected. Many CAD packages offer the hop, a gap or a plain crossing as display options, and the choice is set per drawing set.

The hop carries no physical meaning; it is a reading aid. This illustration is an independent explanation of the convention rather than a reproduction of the IEEE graphic. Where a drawing set mixes hops and plain crossings, check the legend rather than assuming that plain crossings are connected.
readingNotes: Treat the hop as no connection.
Check whether the drawing set also uses plain crossings.
drawingChecklist: Use one crossing display style per drawing set.
Never place a junction dot on a hop.
State the crossing convention in the legend.
distinction: A hop is an unconnected crossing; a junction dot is a connection.
